title: Romeo and Juliet: Character Relationships
subtitle: Follow the loyalties, secrets, and choices that drive the tragedy
overview: Explore a relationship map of Shakespeare's tragedy to understand how family conflict, friendship, secrecy, and urgent decisions shape the plot.
essentialQuestion: How do relationships and failed communication turn private choices into public tragedy?

objectives.title: Identify families and allies
objectives.description: Recognize who belongs to each household and who connects them.

objectives.title: Trace communication
objectives.description: Follow how secret plans and missed messages move between characters.

objectives.title: Compare motivations
objectives.description: Compare how love, loyalty, honor, and authority shape decisions.

objectives.title: Explain cause and effect
objectives.description: Use relationship evidence to explain a turning point in the tragedy.

groups.name: Capulet Household
groups.description: Juliet's family, relatives, and expected match.

groups.name: Bridges and Allies
groups.description: Trusted adults and friends who connect the two households.

characters.name: Romeo Montague
characters.summary: Romeo acts quickly on intense feelings, choosing a secret marriage that crosses the feud between the two households.

characters.name: Mercutio
characters.summary: Mercutio is witty, skeptical about romantic ideals, and fiercely loyal; his death changes the direction of the play.

characters.name: Benvolio Montague
characters.summary: Benvolio repeatedly tries to keep peace, gives Romeo advice, and reports key conflicts to the Prince.

characters.name: Juliet Capulet
characters.summary: Juliet develops an independent plan for her future while facing family authority, secrecy, and rapidly narrowing choices.

characters.name: Tybalt Capulet
characters.summary: Tybalt treats family honor and the feud as urgent duties, turning social tension into a deadly challenge.

characters.name: Lord Capulet
characters.summary: Lord Capulet controls household decisions and presses Juliet to marry Paris when he believes the match will secure her future.

characters.name: Count Paris
characters.summary: Paris seeks to marry Juliet with her father's approval and does not know about her secret marriage to Romeo.

characters.name: Friar Laurence
characters.summary: Friar Laurence secretly marries Romeo and Juliet and later designs a risky plan intended to reunite them and end the feud.

characters.name: The Nurse
characters.summary: The Nurse carries messages for Juliet and offers practical advice, but later recommends a choice that Juliet experiences as betrayal.

relationships.summary: Romeo and Juliet choose a secret marriage across the family feud.
relationships.evidenceSummary: Their meeting, balcony conversation, and secret marriage establish a bond that conflicts with both households' expectations.

relationships.summary: Mercutio is Romeo's loyal and outspoken friend.
relationships.evidenceSummary: Mercutio jokes with Romeo, accompanies him to the Capulet feast, and fights Tybalt after Romeo refuses the challenge.

relationships.summary: Benvolio is Romeo's cousin and trusted companion.
relationships.evidenceSummary: Benvolio listens to Romeo, encourages him to attend the feast, and tries to prevent violent conflict.

relationships.summary: Tybalt is Juliet's cousin and a defender of Capulet honor.
relationships.evidenceSummary: Their family connection places Tybalt's conflict with Romeo inside Juliet's private struggle between love and household loyalty.

relationships.summary: Lord Capulet expects Juliet to obey his marriage decision.
relationships.evidenceSummary: After initially delaying the match, Capulet orders Juliet to marry Paris and reacts angrily when she refuses.

relationships.summary: The Nurse cares for Juliet and becomes her messenger.
relationships.evidenceSummary: The Nurse helps arrange communication with Romeo, then later advises Juliet to marry Paris after Romeo is banished.

relationships.summary: Friar Laurence advises Romeo and agrees to the secret marriage.
relationships.evidenceSummary: The Friar warns Romeo about haste but hopes the marriage may turn family hatred into peace.

relationships.summary: Friar Laurence gives Juliet the sleeping-potion plan.
relationships.evidenceSummary: When Juliet faces marriage to Paris, the Friar proposes a dangerous staged-death plan that depends on a message reaching Romeo.

relationships.summary: Tybalt challenges Romeo in defense of Capulet honor.
relationships.evidenceSummary: Tybalt recognizes Romeo at the feast and later seeks a duel; Romeo refuses because the secret marriage has made Tybalt his kinsman.

relationships.summary: Tybalt fatally wounds Mercutio during the street fight.
relationships.evidenceSummary: Mercutio accepts the conflict Romeo refuses; Tybalt's fatal blow leads Romeo to retaliate and become banished.

relationships.summary: Paris seeks an approved marriage with Juliet.
relationships.evidenceSummary: Paris negotiates with Lord Capulet and believes Juliet will become his wife, but he does not know about her marriage to Romeo.

relationships.summary: Lord Capulet approves Paris as Juliet's husband.
relationships.evidenceSummary: Capulet first asks Paris to win Juliet's affection, then urgently schedules the marriage after Tybalt's death.

missions.title: Find the secret planner
missions.prompt: Select the character who creates a risky plan to reunite the secretly married couple.
hints: Look in the group that bridges both households.

missions.title: Map the Capulet pressure
missions.prompt: Select Juliet, the cousin who defends family honor, and the father who controls her marriage choice.
hints: Look for Juliet, Tybalt, and Lord Capulet.

missions.title: Trace the fragile plan
missions.prompt: Trace the trusted relationships that carry the secret plan from Romeo through Friar Laurence to Juliet.
hints: Both edges connect a young character to the same trusted adult.

missions.title: Compare two urgent choices
missions.prompt: Compare Romeo's and Juliet's motivations when family loyalty conflicts with their secret marriage.
hints: Consider who each person trusts and which consequences each one faces.

missions.title: Explain the turning point
missions.prompt: Explain how the relationships among Romeo, Mercutio, and Tybalt turn a challenge into banishment.
hints: Connect friendship, the refused challenge, Mercutio's death, and Romeo's retaliation.

discussionQuestions: Which character had the best chance to interrupt the tragedy, and what relationship gave them that opportunity?
How does secrecy protect Romeo and Juliet at first but make their situation more dangerous later?

preparedAssessment.prompt: Who carries messages between Juliet and Romeo before the marriage?
Why does Romeo first refuse Tybalt's challenge?
options: The secret marriage has made Tybalt his relative

preparedAssessment.prompt: What makes Friar Laurence's final plan especially fragile?
options: It depends on a message reaching Romeo
It is approved by both families

preparedAssessment.prompt: Compare how the Nurse and Friar Laurence try to help Juliet.
Which relationship most clearly shows how private loyalty can create public consequences?

preparedSummary: You mapped the family loyalties and trusted relationships that cross the feud.
You traced how a secret plan depended on communication between several characters.
You used friendship and conflict to explain the play's major turning point.
